# The Aristocrat Lock

*The Open Table has agreed to open the iron door under the Great Hall, but nobody has ever opened its Aristocrat lock. Ask Leland, the old well-digger who watches the door, to show you the lock, and bring Hex the description.*

    - So the Table argued all night and decided to open the iron door behind the kitchens. I heard Bastian from here. Now they want a lock opened that the Walkers themselves gave up on a hundred years ago. And who do they send for? Riddle me that.
    - Me, of course. But I do not walk to a lock blind. A lock is a question; I want to hear it asked first. What shape, what studs, what wear on the metal, where the old hands touched it most.
    - Go to the Great Hall, *Player*. By the iron door there is an old well-digger called [Leland](../npcs/leland.md) who has been staring at it for longer than is healthy. Have him show you the lock, every inch, and come back and tell me.
    - Look at it the way you would look at a face. The scratches are the expression. Go.

    - Leland, by the iron door in the Great Hall, behind the kitchens. I want the lock described to the last scratch.
    - Hex sent you, did Hex? Good. Come here, bring the lamp. See: no keyhole. Seven iron studs in a ring, like a crown, and a plate in the middle shaped like a key, set into the door and not meant to come out.
    - The third stud and the fifth are worn bright. The others are dull. And the key plate has a scratch round it, as if it was turned, once, against the way you would think. I have dug wells under this city for sixty years and I never saw a lock that looked so pleased with itself.
    - Tell Hex all that. And tell Hex I have rope and lamps ready, for when it opens. If it opens.
    - Seven studs in a crown, a key that is not a key, the third and fifth worn bright, a scratch turned against the sun. Oh, that is lovely. That is an Aristocrat joke. They built a lock that tells you its answer and dares you to believe it.

    - Ha! A hundred years! I could kiss it. I will not, it is filthy. Leland, somebody has to keep this door now, and the Table will name nobody else: you have stared at it longer than anyone alive. Keeper of the Low Door. It suits you.
